answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by rating identities on sustained, useful work instead of cheap signups. A newcomer starts at its nadir, trusted with only tiny supervised tasks, and a hollow profile with no history of real contributions stays capped there no matter how many copies of it appear. When a sudden gale of fresh accounts arrives all behaving identically, peers can spot the burst against the slow, uneven rhythm of genuine agents and freeze the whole cluster before it drains any rewards.
